description: Pollo alla Cacciatora is a beloved Italian classic, a hearty hunter-style chicken dish braised in a rich tomato sauce with bell peppers, onions, and often mushrooms and olives. This rustic recipe brings the flavors of the Italian countryside to your table, offering tender chicken enveloped in a savory, aromatic sauce perfect for a comforting meal. It is a testament to simple ingredients transforming into an extraordinary culinary experience.

ingredients.notes: cut into 8 pieces, or 2-3 lbs chicken thighs/drumsticks

instructions.title: Brown the Chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken pieces dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches until golden on all sides, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Vegetables
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion and bell peppers to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in minced garlic and sliced mushrooms and cook for another 3-5 minutes until mushrooms are tender and fragrant.

instructions.title: Deglaze with Wine
instructions.text: Pour in the dry white wine, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to loosen any browned bits. Let the wine simmer and reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Tomatoes and Broth
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Simmer the Chicken
instructions.text: Return the browned chicken pieces to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure the chicken is mostly submerged. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the pitted Kalamata olives during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Pollo alla Cacciatora is wonderful served with polenta, pasta, or crusty bread.

tips: For richer flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces. The skin can be removed after browning for a lighter dish, but the bones add depth during simmering.
A splash of balsamic vinegar or a pinch of red pepper flakes can be added for an extra layer of flavor and a slight kick.
Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. The flavors often deepen overnight, making it even more delicious the next day.
